newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ hears no more of threatened Iran trade ban.
newsitem.headline: NZ hears no more of threatened Iran trade ban.

text.p: New Zealand has received no confirmation of a reported trade ban imposed by Iran earlier this month, officials said on Monday.
"We have not had anything formal or informal, and basically no news is good news," a spokesman for Foreign Affairs and Trade Minister Don McKinnon said.
New Zealand temporarily withdrew its ambassador from Tehran for consultations on April 11 after a German court ruled that Iran ordered the 1992 murders of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.

The action, part of coordinated international diplomatic action led by European Union countries, seemed to catch the Iranians by surprise. The national news agency IRNA reported trade links were being broken with New Zealand in response.
The situation was left unclear when Iran also withdrew its ambassador, who left New Zealand saying no ban was yet in force.

New Zealand officials were wary of saying the threat had been removed. Asked if trade was continuing, the spokesman said: "I think there have been some people up there recently and they haven't experienced any problems.
"Certainly there have been people in Tehran talking about delivering things and they don't seem to have met any problems."

The director of the Foreign Ministry's Middle East and Africa division, John Hayes, said there had been no communication and New Zealand's ambassador had not had any problems on his subsequent return to Tehran.
